clue.text: Authority covering very old area of France

indicators.note: covering means the first piece wraps round the pieces that follow it

parts.note: to have the say is to have authority

explanation.surface: Some ruling body takes in a historic region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Savoy is a historic region in the south-east of France, bordering Italy and Switzerland.

clue.text: One whose job on the board is character-forming

definitions.text: One whose job on the board is character-forming

parts.words: One whose job on the board is character-forming
parts.note: the board is a shop sign, and the characters are painted letters, not personalities

explanation.definitionFit: A tradesperson who paints lettering on shop fronts and boards.

clue.text: Vehicle sometimes seen beside dyke

definitions.meaning: the word precedes Dyke in names such as Dick ... Dyke

explanation.definitionFit: A van is a road vehicle, and the word comes before Dyke in the actor's surname.

clue.text: Hurt, scream like Kipling's Dog Dingo

parts.note: to yell is to scream
ow is the cry of someone hurt

explanation.surface: Someone in pain cries out like a wild dog.
explanation.walkthrough: In Kipling's Just So Stories the Dingo is 'Yellow-Dog Dingo'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Just So Stories call the Australian wild dog Yellow-Dog Dingo, for its colour.

clue.text: Bird (a knot) breaking into mollusc out East

indicators.note: breaking into means the bracketed pair goes inside the shellfish word
out means the compass point is dropped from the shellfish word

parts.note: a cockle is an edible bivalve mollusc
a tie is a knot, as in tying a rope

explanation.surface: A bird with a knotted rope somehow gets into a shellfish in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' drops the E of the mollusc, and 'breaking into' sets A plus the knot word inside what is left, before its final L.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockatiel is a small crested Australian parrot, a popular cage bird.

clue.text: Names a member's adopted for holiday venues

indicators.note: adopted means taken in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to name sources is to cite them
an MP is a Member of Parliament; MP'S gives the letters

explanation.surface: An MP's chosen words for places to go on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Campsites are places where holidaymakers pitch tents or park caravans.

clue.text: Part of poem leader of synagogue left unfinished

indicators.note: left unfinished means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a cantor leads the singing in a synagogue

explanation.surface: A section of verse that a synagogue singer never completed.
explanation.definitionFit: A canto is one of the main divisions of a long poem, as in Dante.

clue.text: It's used by pilot going over parts of Paris

definitions.text: It's used by pilot going over parts of Paris

indicators.note: going over means in this down clue the pilot word sits above the rest
parts of means the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: an ace is a top fighter pilot

explanation.surface: Something a flyer uses when passing over districts of the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts of' rearranges PARIS to AIRSP; 'going over' sets ACE below it in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Airspace is the region of sky above a territory, which an aircraft uses in flight.

clue.text: Temporary agent put up in dwelling within

indicators.note: in means the reversed piece goes inside the other

parts.note: immanent means indwelling, present within

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent

explanation.surface: A stand-in agent is lodged in a home inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reads the agent upwards in this down light; 'in' then lodges it after the first two letters of the word for dwelling within.
explanation.definitionFit: Impermanent means not lasting, a synonym of temporary.

clue.text: How Pertelote produces literary works?

definitions.meaning: Pertelote is the hen in Chaucer's Nun's Priest's Tale, who produces eggs

explanation.walkthrough: Pertelote is the hen in Chaucer's Nun's Priest's Tale, wife of Chauntecleer the cock.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen produces eggs in this way, and the same word names short narrative poems.

clue.text: Smugglers with a preference for the flaxen-haired?

definitions.meaning: smugglers were euphemistically called the ..., as in Kipling's Smuggler's Song

definitions.text: with a preference for the flaxen-haired
definitions.meaning: from the title ... Prefer Blondes, the novel and Marilyn Monroe film

explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's 'A Smuggler's Song' has 'Watch the wall, my darling, while the Gentlemen go by'.
explanation.definitionFit: Smugglers were called gentlemen in old usage, and the famous title says men of that sort prefer blondes.

clue.text: Come back about thin layer of wood

parts.note: re means about or concerning
ply is one thin sheet in plywood

explanation.surface: Someone is told to return, regarding a sheet of plywood.
explanation.definitionFit: To come back with words is to answer someone, a synonym in the sense of a retort.

clue.text: One may not necessarily purchase lights

definitions.text: One may not necessarily purchase lights

parts.words: One may not necessarily purchase lights
parts.note: lights are windows, and a person who browses goods behind shop glass need not buy anything

explanation.definitionFit: A browser who looks at displays in shop windows without always buying, with lights as the old word for windows.

clue.text: Embroidery depicting feature of Isle of Wight rock?

definitions.text: feature of Isle of Wight rock
definitions.meaning: the Needles are chalk stacks off the Isle of Wight, so one has a sharp tip

explanation.walkthrough: The Needles are a row of chalk stacks off the western tip of the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Needlepoint is canvas embroidery, and a point of one of the Needles is a rock feature.

clue.text: Creature about to enter the worst resort

indicators.note: to enter means one piece goes inside the other
resort means sort again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Some animal is about to go into the worst holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' rearranges THE WORST to OTTERSHW; 'to enter' puts RE in before the final W.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter shrew is a small aquatic African mammal.

clue.text: A couple in the news?

parts.note: a couple romantically linked is said to be one unit, and a news story is one piece of the same name

explanation.definitionFit: Two people dating are called this word, which is also a single report in a newspaper.

clue.text: Express packet possibly required for government business

parts.note: to express something is to state it
a packet is a packet boat, so an example of a seagoing craft

explanation.surface: A parcel sent by express post might be needed for official work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packet' is not a parcel but a packet boat, a mail ship, which is a craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Statecraft is the art of conducting the affairs of government.

clue.text: Weak adhesive what's-its-name

parts.note: thin means weak, as in a thin excuse
gummy means sticky

explanation.surface: Some feeble glue whose name escapes one.
explanation.definitionFit: A thingummy is a placeholder word for something whose name one cannot recall.

clue.text: Niagara River trip to do with land management

indicators.note: trip suggests a stumble, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A journey along the Niagara is a farming matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrarian means relating to cultivated land and its ownership.

clue.text: Continental management mostly expressing lavish praise

parts.note: EU, the European Union, stands for the Continent in crosswords

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: logistics is the management of supplies and operations

explanation.surface: Executives across the Channel are usually full of fulsome compliments.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogy is a speech of high praise, so the adjective describes extravagant commendation.

clue.text: Jarrow monk's contribution to rosary, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a bead is one of the small balls strung on a rosary

explanation.surface: A Northumbrian monk adds his bit to the string of prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venerable Bede was the Anglo-Saxon historian who lived at the monastery of Jarrow.

clue.text: Dead queen buried in cold southern port

indicators.note: buried in means placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
Queen Anne is dead, from the saying Queen Anne's dead

explanation.surface: A departed monarch lies interred in a chilly harbour town in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen Anne's dead' is an old retort to stale news, so a dead queen is ANNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannes is a port on the French Riviera.

clue.text: Insect settling across river: it's on an island

indicators.note: on means the second piece is placed after the island word
across means the settling word is laid over and round the river letter

parts.note: settling a bill is paying it
the Isle of Man is the crossword island
'tis is the old contraction for it is

explanation.surface: Some bug comes to rest over a river on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' lays the settling word over the river letter; 'on' places the old contraction after the island. The Isle of Man lies between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The praying mantis is a predatory insect that holds its forelegs as if in prayer.

clue.text: Silver penny missing? It makes us very angry

indicators.note: missing means the letter is left out

parts.note: Long John Silver is the pirate in Treasure Island

explanation.surface: A missing silver coin is the thing that infuriates us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silver' is not the metal but Long John Silver, a pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate means extremely angry or furious.

clue.text: Soon after midday son imbibed sparkling wine

indicators.note: imbibed means taken in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: at one o'clock, written AT I with the Roman numeral, is soon after noon

explanation.surface: Just past noon a boy drank fizzy wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont in Italy.

clue.text: Wells's writing rejected in specific situations

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something H G Wells wrote is turned down in particular circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: IFICS sits inside 'specific situations'; 'rejected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: H G Wells wrote early science fiction such as The War of the Worlds and The Time Machine.

clue.text: Carpet and reportedly sack politician wasting current

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so a word with the same sound

parts.note: to sack someone is to axe them

indicators.note: wasting means a letter is lost from the politician word

parts.note: a minister is a senior politician
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone wants to dismiss a politician who squanders the flow.
explanation.definitionFit: Axminster is a type of woven carpet, named after the Devon town where it was first made.

clue.text: Jack's initially reluctant to join army

parts.note: the TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter

explanation.surface: A man is hesitant at first to enlist.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack tar is old slang for a sailor, so jack and tar both mean a seaman.

clue.text: Style in' north-east abandoned with deep feeling

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion followed in the north-east has been dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something intensely is to do it with great force of emotion.

clue.text: It's clutched at in desperation when verrucas return

indicators.note: return means the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: verrucas are warts on the foot

explanation.surface: A drowning-man image meets a foot complaint coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: A drowning man clutches at straws: the definition is the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says a desperate person will clutch at any flimsy hope, pictured as a stalk of dried grass.
